description:
File: crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:33 and crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:20
Issue: SetError and SetErrorType are fully redefined in jmap-mail-server instead of re-exporting or extending the type from jmap-server. The two structs are structurally similar but not the same Rust type. Mail-specific fields (max_recipients, invalid_recipients, not_found, max_size) could not be added to the base type so a parallel definition was introduced. These two types cannot be used interchangeably — code that imports one cannot accept the other — and there is no compiler error when a new variant is added to one but not the other.
Risk: Adding a new base RFC 8620 SetError variant requires editing two places (jmap-server and every domain crate). Missing the update in one crate compiles silently. As jmap-chat-server re-exports SetError from jmap-server, it diverges from jmap-mail-server consumers, creating an inconsistent API surface across the crate family.
Fix: Either (a) merge all fields into the base SetError in jmap-server (mail-specific fields are skip_serializing_if = None so they add no wire cost for non-mail types), or (b) define a MailSetError that wraps/extends the base type and document the extension pattern explicitly for future domain crates.
title: Dual SetError/SetErrorType definitions
